request: Brokers want debit-order and payroll clients to be able to choose "last day of the month" as their collection day, instead of being limited to days 1 to 28.

summary.business: Today a monthly debit order or payroll deduction can only be collected on days 1 to 28. That limit was added on 20 September after collections on the 31st bounced in shorter months (INC-2291). This change adds a "last day of the month" option so the collection moves with the month: 28 or 29 February, 30 April, 31 May. It touches two process steps (capturing collection details and validating), the database, and the screens and API brokers use. The biggest open question is outside this codebase: whatever system actually sends the debit order to the bank must understand the new option, or the September incident will repeat.
summary.technical: Add a CollectsOnLastDay flag to CollectionInstruction (entity, schema delta 004, DbContractRepository persistence) rather than overloading CollectionDay with a sentinel value. IsValidCollectionDay() accepts the flag for recurring methods (DEBIT_ORDER, PAYROLL); NB-COLLECTION-002 messaging changes accordingly. Carry the flag through CollectionInstructionRequest, CollectionService and NewBusinessService via a new overload so ICollectionService's existing signature and its callers stay intact. Expose an effective-date helper so downstream collections never has to interpret the flag themselves.

questions: Does "last day" mean the last calendar day, or the last business day? Banks will not process a debit order on a Sunday, so 31 May 2026 would roll to Monday 1 June unless we say otherwise.
Which system builds the monthly debit-order file for the bank? It is not in this repo, and it must honour the new flag.
Should the existing contracts still carrying day 29, 30 or 31 (left over from before the INC-2291 fix) be converted to "last day"? If so, who approves the conversion and do clients need to be told?
Should one-off methods (EFT, CARD, CASH) also offer "last day", or only recurring monthly methods?
Does Finance need the collection day or the new flag on the nightly contract-status CSV?

tables.detail: CollectsOnLastDay (logical, initial no). CollectionDay keeps its current meaning.

risks.title: The bank file may ignore the new option and repeat INC-2291
risks.why: INC-2291 happened because a collection day did not exist in every month. The system that builds the debit-order run is outside this repo, so nothing here proves it will read CollectsOnLastDay. If it only reads CollectionDay, a last-day client would be collected on whatever placeholder day is stored.
risks.mitigation: Confirm the consumer before build. Give it GetCollectionDateFor() or a pre-computed date rather than the raw flag.

risks.title: Reusing CollectionDay as a code (0 or 99) would break an existing regression test
risks.why: Evaluate_Fails_WhenCollectionDayIsZero asserts that day 0 is invalid, and DbContractRepository stores the day as a plain integer. A sentinel value changes the meaning of a field every consumer already reads.
risks.mitigation: Use a separate logical field (recommended in this plan).

risks.title: Merge requests will not run the ABLUnit suite
risks.why: Since NBJ-138, compile and test jobs only run when OE_RUNNER is true. Without a self-hosted OpenEdge runner, this change can merge with only the repository-structure check passing.
risks.mitigation: Run the suite locally and attach results to the MR, or enable an OpenEdge runner before this work starts.

risks.title: Changing the service interface ripples to every caller
risks.why: ICollectionService.CaptureCollection and NewBusinessService.SetCollectionInstruction are called from the controller, NewBusinessServiceTest and EdgeCaseTest. Changing their signatures breaks compilation in all of them.
risks.mitigation: Add overloads; keep the existing signatures delegating with the flag set to FALSE.

risks.title: Converting old day 29-31 contracts will force re-validation
risks.why: Any change to a contract after Validate() makes its validation stale (Edge Case 47). NEW contracts converted in bulk will be refused at activation until re-validated, which is the confusion already seen in INC-2311.
risks.mitigation: Convert only IN-FORCE contracts in the migration, or re-run validation for converted NEW contracts and tell supervisors.

risks.title: Adding the flag to the status report changes the Finance CSV
risks.why: ttContractStatus.i drives both the API and the nightly CSV. The last layout change broke the Finance import.
risks.mitigation: Leave the report unchanged unless Finance asks, and agree the new layout with them first.

risks.title: The persistence code has no direct tests
risks.why: DbContractRepository has no test that references it directly, so a mistake mapping the new field to the database would only show up in a PASOE environment.
risks.mitigation: Add a round-trip test against a test database, or verify manually on the CI schema database.

tests.name: Evaluate_Passes_WhenDebitOrderUsesLastDayOfMonth
tests.purpose: A monthly debit order set to the last day of the month passes NB-COLLECTION-002.
tests.code:
@Test.
    METHOD PUBLIC VOID Evaluate_Passes_WhenDebitOrderUsesLastDayOfMonth ( ):
        DEFINE VARIABLE oRule        AS CollectionDateRequiredRule NO-UNDO.
        DEFINE VARIABLE oContract    AS Contract                    NO-UNDO.
        DEFINE VARIABLE oInstruction AS CollectionInstruction       NO-UNDO.
        DEFINE VARIABLE oResult      AS ValidationResult            NO-UNDO.

        oContract = NEW Contract().
        oContract:Create("CON-TEST-060", "test").

        oInstruction = NEW CollectionInstruction().
        oInstruction:Create("CON-TEST-060", CollectionInstruction:METHOD_DEBIT_ORDER, 0, "123456", "001", "John Doe", "test").
        oInstruction:UseLastDayOfMonth().
        oContract:SetCollectionInstruction(oInstruction).

        oRule   = NEW CollectionDateRequiredRule().
        oResult = oRule:Evaluate(oContract).

        Assert:IsTrue(oResult:IsValid, "DEBIT_ORDER on the last day of the month should pass").
    END METHOD.

tests.name: Evaluate_StillFails_WhenDebitOrderDayIs31WithoutLastDayOption
tests.purpose: Guards the INC-2291 fix: choosing day 31 explicitly is still rejected.
tests.code:
@Test.
    METHOD PUBLIC VOID Evaluate_StillFails_WhenDebitOrderDayIs31WithoutLastDayOption ( ):
        DEFINE VARIABLE oRule        AS CollectionDateRequiredRule NO-UNDO.
        DEFINE VARIABLE oContract    AS Contract                    NO-UNDO.
        DEFINE VARIABLE oInstruction AS CollectionInstruction       NO-UNDO.
        DEFINE VARIABLE oResult      AS ValidationResult            NO-UNDO.

        oContract = NEW Contract().
        oContract:Create("CON-TEST-061", "test").

        oInstruction = NEW CollectionInstruction().
        oInstruction:Create("CON-TEST-061", CollectionInstruction:METHOD_DEBIT_ORDER, 31, "123456", "001", "John Doe", "test").
        oContract:SetCollectionInstruction(oInstruction).

        oRule   = NEW CollectionDateRequiredRule().
        oResult = oRule:Evaluate(oContract).

        Assert:IsFalse(oResult:IsValid, "Day 31 without the last-day option must still fail").
        Assert:Equals("NB-COLLECTION-002", oResult:RuleCode).
    END METHOD.

tests.name: GetCollectionDateFor_ReturnsMonthEnd
tests.purpose: The calculated date is correct for February (leap and non-leap), a 30-day and a 31-day month.
tests.code:
@Test.
    METHOD PUBLIC VOID GetCollectionDateFor_ReturnsMonthEnd ( ):
        DEFINE VARIABLE oInstruction AS CollectionInstruction NO-UNDO.

        oInstruction = NEW CollectionInstruction().
        oInstruction:Create("CON-TEST-063", CollectionInstruction:METHOD_DEBIT_ORDER, 0, "123456", "001", "John Doe", "test").
        oInstruction:UseLastDayOfMonth().

        Assert:Equals(DATE(2, 28, 2027), oInstruction:GetCollectionDateFor(DATE(2, 1, 2027))).
        Assert:Equals(DATE(2, 29, 2028), oInstruction:GetCollectionDateFor(DATE(2, 10, 2028))).
        Assert:Equals(DATE(4, 30, 2027), oInstruction:GetCollectionDateFor(DATE(4, 1, 2027))).
        Assert:Equals(DATE(5, 31, 2027), oInstruction:GetCollectionDateFor(DATE(5, 15, 2027))).
    END METHOD.
